questions.q: 'I did not know that she ___ a doctor.' is or was?
questions.a: 'was' — the main clause is past, so the fact-about-her steps back. A wrong answer 'is' shows the student missed the time-zone rule — though 'is' can defend if she still is one, boards expect 'was'.

questions.q: 'The teacher explained that the sun ___ in the east.' rise/rises/rose?
questions.a: 'rises' — universal truth exempt from backshift. A wrong answer 'rose' shows mechanical shifting without the exemption — the competent-but-rigid error.

questions.q: 'When I was young, I believed that stars ___ tiny lamps.' are/were?
questions.a: 'were' — the belief was false, so no truth-exemption applies; the past zone governs. A wrong answer 'are' misapplies the exemption to a mistaken belief.

questions.q: Sequence of tenses: when a sentence has two clauses, the tense of the second is ______ by the first.
Fill in the blank: Sequence of tenses: when a sentence has two clauses, the tense of the second is ______ by the first.
Fill in the blank: The anchor rule: the main verb sets the time-zone; ______ verbs must live inside it. 'I think she IS right' / 'I thought she WAS right'.
What is Sequence of tenses? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Sequence of tenses: when a sentence has two clauses, the tense of the second is constrained by the first.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Sequence of tenses?
questions.a: Students shift every verb blindly after a past main clause — including facts that are still true — or fail to shift at all, writing 'He said he is busy'.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student aligns subordinate-clause tense with the main-clause tense in object clauses, time clauses, and purpose clauses, including the universal-truth exemption.
